content.title: About
content.content: Gin is a distilled spirit made from grain alcohol flavored with juniper berries and a variety of other botanicals. It has a distinctive piney aroma and is a staple base for many classic cocktails.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “gin” derives from the English “juniper,” the primary botanical used for flavoring.
The first gin, known as “genever,” originated in the Netherlands in the 17th century before becoming popular in England.
Classic London Dry Gin contains no sugar after distillation, giving it a dry, clean taste.
There are over 100 styles of gin, each differing in the blend of botanicals.
Gin is a key ingredient in cocktails such as the Martini, Gimlet, and Tom Collins.

items.title: Antioxidant properties of juniper
items.content: Juniper essential oils contain antioxidants that may help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Botanicals like coriander and angelica traditionally support digestion and relieve bloating.

items.title: Stress reduction
items.content: Moderate consumption can promote relaxation thanks to aromatic compounds.

items.title: Alcohol intoxication
items.content: Gin typically has a high alcohol content (40 % ABV or higher), so it should be enjoyed in moderation.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Alcohol can amplify the effects of sedatives and certain antibiotics.

items.title: Allergy to botanicals
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to juniper or other herbs used in gin.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Gin is often served chilled neat, but most commonly it is mixed in cocktails. The classic “gin & tonic” with a lime wedge is a popular choice. Gin can also be added to marinades, sauces, or desserts for a botanical twist.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bottle in a cool, dark place with the cap tightly sealed. Properly stored gin retains its flavor profile for many years.
